runtimeChoice.decision: Node.js runtime via Vercel's Fastify framework entrypoint detection (the zero-configuration path)

verifiedDocumentation.whatItSays: "This file should be created in your project's root directory" (vercel.json placement). The functions property: "A glob pattern that matches the paths of the Vercel functions you would like to customize"; its runtime value is "The npm package name of a Runtime, including its version" and is documented ONLY under "Using unsupported runtimes" ("To use a runtime that is not officially supported, you can add a runtime property" — the example is vercel-php@0.5.2). The Bun runtime is configured by the TOP-LEVEL bunVersion property ("The bunVersion property configures your project to use the Bun runtime instead of Node.js"; values "1.4.x" | "1.x"), NOT through functions.runtime.

The Bun runtime page carries "🔒 Permissions Required: The Bun runtime (Beta)". The sanctioned Bun shapes are Bun.serve() entrypoints (the framework preset: bunVersion + bun.lock + a server entrypoint in the project root or src/, calling Bun.serve() once during module startup; or api/server.ts served at /api/server with prefix-related routing caveats). The framework-specific guidance covers only Next.js. No Fastify-on-Bun entrypoint shape is documented.

"Fastify entrypoint detection": the entry "should be named one of the following": src/app.{js,mjs,cjs,ts,cts,mts}, src/index.{...}, src/server.{...}, app.{...}, index.{...}, server.{...} — "Create your Fastify instance, register your routes, and call fastify.listen() in this file." The whole app becomes a single Vercel Function on Fluid compute (Node.js runtime by default).

"Because your app is deployed as one function, Vercel routes every incoming request to it and lets Fastify's router match the path." — the original-path guarantee for the route table at its ROOT paths (no /api folder, no rewrites needed).

"Vercel's framework-defined infrastructure now recognizes and deeply understands Express applications. This update removes the need for redirects in vercel.json or using the /api folder." — the framework-detection shape supersedes the api/-folder + rewrite pattern for backend frameworks.

VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_REF — "Available at: Both build and runtime" — "The git branch of the commit the deployment was triggered by." (Consumed by the adapter as the preview-branch input — the only host-specific variable; every identity input stays the governed ZECK_* contract.)
Maximum duration with Fluid compute, Node.js/Bun/Python runtimes: Hobby "300s (5 minutes)" default and maximum — the vercel.json maxDuration bound (60) stays within it.

mechanicalVerification: The npm package @vercel/frameworks@3.34.0 (the framework detection definitions Vercel's build uses) was fetched and inspected: the Fastify framework definition has detectors {every: [matchPackage fastify]} + entry files [app, index, server, src/app, src/index, src/server] x [js, cjs, mjs, ts, cts, mts] matched by the content regex importing fastify; useRuntime {@vercel/fastify}; defaultRoutes [{handle: filesystem}, {src: '/(.*)', dest: '/', transforms: [{type: request.path, op: set, args: '/$1'}]}] — the platform routing that preserves the ORIGINAL path for Fastify's router.

The npm package @vercel/fastify@8.0.1 (dist/index.js) was fetched and inspected: it delegates to @vercel/node's build with an entrypointCallback that searches exactly those root/src entry filenames whose content imports fastify.

The npm package @vercel/node@13.0.1 (dist/bundling-handler.js + dist/index.js) was fetched and inspected: the runtime "Monkey-patch[s] http.Server.prototype.listen to capture server instances created during module import (e.g. Express apps calling app.listen())" — the module loads ONCE per entrypoint (handlerCache: "concurrent requests to the same entrypoint share one compileUserCode() call"), the captured Fastify server is bound to 127.0.0.1:0 once and every request is proxied into it with "path: req.url" (the ORIGINAL request path). The builder consumes the vercel.json functions config via "config.functions?.[entrypoint]" keyed by the relative entrypoint path — for the root entry that key is "server.ts", which is the glob vercel.json uses.

The official example repository github.com/vercel/vercel/tree/main/examples/fastify was fetched: it contains exactly package.json + server.ts (root, importing fastify, calling fastify.listen({port: 3000})) + tsconfig.json — the shape this delivery follows.
runtimeChoice.reasoning: The work order asked for the sanctioned Bun runtime function configuration (vercel.json functions runtime field) with the Node.js runtime acceptable if Bun does not fit. Verification found: (1) the functions.runtime field does NOT carry the Bun runtime in current documentation — it is reserved for runtimes that are not officially supported (community npm packages); the sanctioned Bun configuration is the top-level bunVersion; (2) the Bun runtime is Beta and permissions-gated and its documented entrypoint shapes are Bun.serve() servers with Next.js as the only framework-specific guidance — no Fastify shape; (3) the Fastify framework detection (root server.ts + fastify.listen) is the CURRENT dedicated zero-configuration path for exactly this transport, on the Node.js runtime, with the original-path routing explicitly documented. Node.js chosen per the work order's allowance; the Bun option (bunVersion) is recorded here for the Lead.

LEAD DEPLOYMENT-RUN ADDENDUM (2026-09-21, the credentialed run this record's notRun row owned): the first three live deployment attempts on the Vercel project zeck-preview-main (team ekonplacidegmailcoms-projects) proved TWO platform facts the worker sandbox could not observe, both corrected in the same run: (1) the platform build REJECTS the functions-key entry pattern for a root entry — vercel.json's functions["server.ts"] fails with 'The pattern "server.ts" defined in `functions` doesn't match any Serverless Functions inside the `api` directory' (reproduced with and without an explicit framework pin; the corrected vercel.json pins framework: fastify only, and the build's default file tracing ships deploy/manifests/*.json into the function bundle — verified in the locally-built .vercel/output/functions bundle via `vercel build`); (2) the sandbox build's tsc transpile cannot resolve a `types` pin from the repository tsconfig.json (TS2688 'Cannot find type definition file for node' even with @types/node@26.4.0 present in the bun install output) — the corrected tsconfig carries no `types` array; the Lead re-verified typecheck 0 errors, lint 68w/8i/0e (house baseline) and the unit suite on the real rail after the change. The hosting-contract unit test was re-pinned to the corrected contract. The deployment itself then hit the team's free-tier 100-deployments-per-day quota (96 consumed by the operator's other active projects in the rolling window) — a hard provider boundary, not a build defect; the corrected build is verified locally and the deployment retries when the rolling window frees a slot.
